Assistant: Well first you have to make some ice cream, which is in itself quite an accomplishment.  You can make it from scratch or with a cream to custard base, but I recommend the former.  Here’s what you’ll need:

- 2 cups of whole milk

- 1 cup of heavy cream, the kind that’s in the “cream” section of your grocery store (I prefer a blend of both whole milk and heavy cream, mostly because I find the latter easier to whip)

- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

- 1/4 teaspoon salt

- 1 tablespoon sugar

- 2 tablespoons cornstarch, sifted

- 2 tablespoons butter, melted

- Ice cream freezer, or room temperature

- Chopped fruit or nuts, like chocolate chips, kiwi, or candied ginger, to serve on top.

Now here’s what you do.  First you make the ice cream base by whisking the milk and cream, and vanilla extract into a bowl, and then whisking in two tablespoons of sugar and one tablespoon of cornstarch.  You can also add just the sugar if you’d like.  The cornstarch doesn’t actually need to be completely dissolved, I usually leave it in as flakes in a layer on top that will dissolve in the next step.  The mixture needs to be very smooth after that, it’s quite tricky to make it runny.  The heat of the milk and cream will make the cornstarch dissolve, but it’s best if you whisk the whole thing together very thoroughly to get out as much of the liquid as possible.  Next, add the butter and mix with a whisk until it’s melted, but make sure that it’s not too hot, if it starts to boil it’s all been cooked through.

Now it’s time to chill the mixture.  Add it to a container with a lid and place it in the fridge for at least an hour, preferably overnight.  It’s important not to stir it or touch it in any way, the cornstarch in the mixture will dissolve and you’ll end up with a cloudy, lumpy mess.  You can add the sugar to the mixture to help the cornstarch dissolve, though it will only help a little, it won’t matter.  The milk and cream will also take a few days to “cure” and thicken into a solid solid, so you may not get any ice cream for a couple of weeks, at least.  Finally, you’ll need to churn the mixture to make it ice cream.  Churning is really easy, you just put a container with the ice cream mixture in it in the freezer, then take it out, and stir it up with a fork or the back of a spoon, moving it back and forth over the surface.  Churn the mixture for two hours or until the center is firm, you can stop when you want to, or keep on churning until it’s completely done.  When it’s finished, you can store it in a cool place for a week or two.  One final thing, I’d recommend waiting until you’re ready to eat it to put it in the freezer, otherwise it’ll get mushy and it won’t be as good when it’s out there.
